concepts.name: Tables, rows and columns
concepts.summary: Recognise that relational data is stored in tables of rows (records) and typed columns (fields) and describe what each represents.

concepts.name: Primary and foreign keys
concepts.summary: Explain how a primary key uniquely identifies a row and how a foreign key references another table to link related data.

concepts.name: SELECT and FROM
concepts.summary: Read and explain a query that retrieves chosen columns from a table, including the meaning of SELECT *.

concepts.name: Filtering with WHERE
concepts.summary: Understand that WHERE keeps only rows satisfying a condition built from comparison operators.

concepts.name: Sorting with ORDER BY
concepts.summary: Explain how ORDER BY sorts result rows ascending or descending by one or more columns.

concepts.name: Common data types
concepts.summary: Recall the main column data types (integer, decimal, text, date/time, boolean) and what kind of value each stores.

misconceptions.text: A SQL table has a guaranteed row order, so rows come back in the order they were inserted without ORDER BY.
SELECT changes or removes the data in the table it reads from.
A foreign key column must contain unique values just like a primary key.

concepts.name: Compound conditions with AND/OR
concepts.summary: Combine conditions using AND, OR, NOT and parentheses so the intended rows are selected.

concepts.name: Pattern, range and set predicates
concepts.summary: Use LIKE, BETWEEN and IN to filter on text patterns, ranges and lists of values.

concepts.name: NULL handling
concepts.summary: Test for missing values with IS NULL and understand that comparisons with NULL are neither true nor false.

concepts.name: Aggregate functions
concepts.summary: Compute COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX over a set of rows to answer summary questions.

concepts.name: Grouping with GROUP BY
concepts.summary: Produce one summary row per group by combining GROUP BY with aggregate functions.

concepts.name: Inserting, updating and deleting rows
concepts.summary: Add, change and remove records using INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, with a WHERE clause to limit the affected rows.

concepts.name: Aliases and DISTINCT
concepts.summary: Rename columns and tables with aliases and remove duplicate result rows with DISTINCT.

concepts.name: Inner joins on keys
concepts.summary: Combine rows from two tables by matching a foreign key to a primary key using JOIN ... ON.

misconceptions.text: WHERE column = NULL finds rows with missing values.
UPDATE or DELETE without a WHERE clause only affects one row.
Any selected column can appear alongside aggregates in a GROUP BY query without being grouped.

concepts.name: Outer joins and unmatched rows
concepts.summary: Use LEFT, RIGHT and FULL joins to keep unmatched rows and identify them via NULLs.

concepts.name: Filtering groups with HAVING
concepts.summary: Filter aggregated groups with HAVING and distinguish it from row-level filtering with WHERE.

concepts.name: Logical order of query evaluation
concepts.summary: Analyse why clauses are evaluated in the order FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY and predict what aliases and filters are visible where.

concepts.name: Subqueries in WHERE and FROM
concepts.summary: Write scalar, list and table subqueries and decide when a nested query answers a question better than a join.

concepts.name: Correlated subqueries and EXISTS
concepts.summary: Use correlated subqueries and EXISTS to test for related rows, and compare them with joins.

concepts.name: Set operations
concepts.summary: Combine compatible result sets with UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT and EXCEPT.

concepts.name: Self joins and multi-table joins
concepts.summary: Model hierarchies and comparisons within one table and chain several joins, including many-to-many link tables.

concepts.name: Expressions and CASE
concepts.summary: Use CASE, COALESCE and string, numeric and date functions to derive values inside queries.

misconceptions.text: HAVING and WHERE are interchangeable, so any condition can go in either.
A column alias defined in SELECT can be used in the WHERE clause of the same query.
Filtering on the right-hand table in the WHERE clause of a LEFT JOIN still preserves unmatched left rows.

concepts.name: Window functions
concepts.summary: Compute rankings, running totals and per-partition values with OVER, PARTITION BY and ORDER BY without collapsing rows.

concepts.name: Common table expressions
concepts.summary: Structure complex queries into named, readable steps with CTEs and judge when they beat nested subqueries.

concepts.name: Recursive queries
concepts.summary: Traverse hierarchical or graph-like data using recursive CTEs with an anchor and a recursive member.

concepts.name: Indexes and query performance
concepts.summary: Evaluate how indexes speed reads, slow writes and are used or ignored depending on the predicates.

concepts.name: Reading execution plans
concepts.summary: Interpret execution plans to find scans, join strategies and costly steps, then judge rewrites.

concepts.name: Transactions and ACID
concepts.summary: Group statements into transactions and analyse how atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability protect data.

concepts.name: Constraints and normalisation
concepts.summary: Judge schema designs using normal forms and enforce integrity with primary, foreign, unique, check and not-null constraints.

concepts.name: Rewriting queries for correctness
concepts.summary: Detect and fix wrong results caused by join fan-out, duplicate counting and NULL semantics, and evaluate equivalent formulations.

misconceptions.text: Window functions and GROUP BY do the same thing and both collapse rows.
Adding more indexes always makes the database faster.
A CTE always materialises results and is therefore always faster than a subquery.

concepts.name: Isolation levels and concurrency anomalies
concepts.summary: Evaluate which isolation level prevents which anomalies and its trade-offs for throughput and correctness in a given workload.

concepts.name: Locking and deadlock design
concepts.summary: Assess locking behaviour and design access patterns that avoid contention and deadlocks.

concepts.name: Optimiser behaviour and statistics
concepts.summary: Judge how statistics and cardinality estimates drive plan choice and diagnose bad plans from misestimates.

concepts.name: Schema and index design for workloads
concepts.summary: Design schemas, composite, covering and partial indexes, and partitioning tailored to a specific read/write workload.

concepts.name: Denormalisation and analytical modelling
concepts.summary: Create dimensional or denormalised models for analytics and justify the departure from normal forms.

concepts.name: Safe large-scale data changes
concepts.summary: Plan batched, idempotent and reversible bulk modifications and schema migrations that limit locking and risk.

concepts.name: SQL injection defence and access control
concepts.summary: Evaluate code and permission setups for injection risk and apply parameterised statements and least-privilege roles.

concepts.name: Dialect portability and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate which SQL features are standard versus engine-specific and choose approaches balancing portability and capability.

misconceptions.text: The SERIALIZABLE isolation level should always be used because it is simply the safest and costs nothing.
Escaping quotes by hand is as reliable as using parameterised queries.
The optimiser always finds the best plan, so query shape and statistics never matter.
